phrases.inText: spend about thirty years of your life
phrases.meaning: pass that many years of your life
memory that keeps things for a long time
put something back in its usual place

examples: If you live until you are ninety, you will spend about thirty years of your life asleep.
If you drink coffee late, you will find it hard to sleep.

discovery.question: Which verb form comes after “if”, and which comes in the other part?
options: Present after if, will + verb in the result
will after if, present in the result
Past after if, would in the result
discovery.explanation: First conditional: if + present simple, will + verb, for real or likely situations.

examples: In one study, students who slept after learning a list of words remembered far more of them the next day than students who stayed awake.
A short walk is far better than another hour on your phone.

discovery.question: What do “far” and “even” do to “more”?
options: They make the difference bigger or stronger
They change it into a question
discovery.explanation: far, much and even make a comparative stronger.
